newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA's Thompson sees steady growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: RBA's Thompson sees steady growth, low inflation.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) deputy governor Graeme Thompson on Thursday described the current condition of the Australian economy as showing steady growth with low inflation.
"A steadily growing economy with low inflation," Thompson said, describing to reporters the benign macro-economic conditions for bank lending.
"We don't have asset price booms as we did with commercial property in particular and the stock market in the 1980s," the deputy governor said.
Australia's gross domestic product seasonally adjusted rose 0.9 percent in the March quarter from the previous quarter to stand 2.4 percent above its level a year earlier.

Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said in May that since March 1993, Australia's cumulative annual average inflation had not exceeded 2.5 percent. The consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the March quarter, leaving annual inflation at 1.3 percent. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
